_doc: OPS profile for the GLOBAL motus-ops-sweep engine — gates the machine that runs the machines on THIS machine: the brain-host orchestrator's schedules, the dream-cycle's step log, Crystal Core's nightly, and the transcript/artifact sources every digest and dashboard count depends on. Personal-machine ops config (paths are ~-absolute, like fleet.json); the engine is dimension-registered in motus-sweep/dimensions.json.

stepLogs._why: The logs dir mixes families (lint-/consolidate-/drift- prefixed reports); only the main <date>.md is the step log.

Crystal Core's nightly (LaunchAgent com.jingshi.crystal-nightly, 04:15) logs to ~/Library/Logs/crystal/nightly.log, which has no ## sections and quotes Jing's words. captureCmd's first command, bin/crystal-nightly-status.py, reads that log, launchd, ~/crystal/backups and ~/crystal/judgments/pending (read-only) and writes this derived step log, one section per check: fresh-run (a run in the last 26h, done exit 0/0, chain ok, refold identical), launchd (last exit code 0), backup (log-<today|yesterday>.db), judge (no failed answers), pending (none older than 48h). Times, exit codes and counts only. A failing check is an O2 block; override it as crystal-nightly#<check>.

sources._why: Codex moved to ChatGPT-app cloud threads 2026-07-04 — no local artifacts. Advisory keeps the gap visible until the local surface returns or a cloud poller lands (wiki: codex/codex-session-store-migration-breaks-jsonl-readers).

The engine reads a step-log dir with no matching file as clean, so without this a capture that skipped bin/crystal-nightly-status.py would pass the crystal-nightly checks on a missing or old file. Each captureCmd rewrites it seconds before the ops capture.
